profile.headline: Software Engineer at People.Inc (Formerly Dotdash Meredith)
profile.summary:
Caught between feeling both incredibly old and completely new to the world of software engineering, as it pertains to web development, I would define myself with the inspired words of Spiderman-- a friendly neighborhood web developer. 

I reminisce on my early days of learning JQuery and Angular 1-3, and being completely impressed by the power of site-builder CMS systems such as WordPress or Drupal, or even the starting point of many web developers, MySpace page customization.

Given that I've been in the professional arena for an ongoing 8+ years now, my perceptions on where our future lies technologically drives me. I have a soft-spot for EdTech, but I have an insatiable hunger for technological innovation that brings life and tech together in a healthy symbiosis.

My current passion is to explore biomimicry and do everything in my being to learn and develop Augmented-Virtual Reality solutions for the future as I believe that is our next era in technological innovation.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: New York City Metropolitan Area · Hybrid
positions.description:
At People.Inc (Formally Dotdash Meredith), I champion the evolving tech landscape by designing and building developer tools and headline features that support multiple publishing subsidiaries. 

Recently, I built a redesigned UI for our inline video UI to be shipped on all of our brands—delivering a flexible, performance‑optimized solution that now anchors our flagship sites. In parallel, I’ve led major refactoring initiatives including one that required porting over and upgrading our VUE-based recipes testimonial app into our microservice ecosystem. 

My focus these days has been accelerating revenue through improvements to pre-roll video and developing and using AI workflows to handoff deliverables even faster.

Working closely with cross-functional teams, I balance pragmatic engineering with a developer-first mindset—prioritizing clean code, reusable components, and iterative delivery. Through this role, I’ve further honed my ability to embrace emerging frameworks, collaborate across disciplines, and shape tools that directly impact user experience and operational efficiency.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Played a major role in migrating our then on-premises site to the AWS cloud infrastructure. 
Built the frontend for the main landing page.
Built several features for our user login release in October 2020, and created several dynamic, BEM-formatted  SASS mixins that have helped cut code redundancy and compiled bundle sizes. Been an integral part in writing the backend for our app Puku with Python-based Lambda functions to manipulate DynamoDB databases, and have made many changes to the site to comply with WCAG-accessibility standards.
positions.insights: Skills: Software Development · Application Programming Interfaces (API) · Full-Stack Development · Figma (Software) · Python · AWS Lambda · AWS RDS · Amazon EC2 · Amazon S3 · JavaScript · React.js

positions.title: Contract Web Developer
positions.description:
As a contract web developer at Access Intelligence, I've had to take on both full-stack development and UX/UI roles. I've built custom search functionality for several sites using Salesforce, designed assets and mocks for over a dozen Wordpress-based award pages with Adobe Illustrator and Sketch respectively, built several custom Wordpress pages using Vagrant, CodeKit, React, and Webpack during development, and have incorporated Git into developer-group’s workflow. 

Access Intelligence has provided me the means to stretch my capabilities as both developer and designer and I can truly say I've enjoyed the culmination of working in both environments.

positions.title: Freelance Web Developer
positions.description:
As a freelance web developer I was responsible for setting up the infrastructure to build the new FDC-Global and PowerGrid website. I created the updated "flat" logo as well as the following: 

• Analyzed the current static website built in HTML and CSS
• Developed the Wordpress site using PHP 7, Built custom parallax themes using HTML, SASS, Javascript. 
• Implemented SEO by incorporating third party plugins. 
• Built a customizable modular design to automate design tweaks by product team with BEM methodology
• Implemented custom image compression logic so High quality images do not lose the quality when they are compressed
• Configured Git version control using Bitbucket repository
• Established a development environment with sub-domains for dev work, staging, and live product
• Created responsive mobile-first wireframes to be implemented
• Developed contemporary design systems that would drive the new website traffic with Sketch and Craft

positions.title: Graduate Assistant
positions.description:
Served as co-project coordinator for NYIT + CITYarts Lincoln Square Holiday Tree 3D ornament project collaboration in which I: 
• Organized a system that would serve as our file management (Google Drive) 
• Built relationships between the students and our new facility for 3-D printing -NYIT's H.I.V.E. (Home of Innovation, Visualization, and Exploration) 
• Assisted HIVE employees by extruding the graphic design student's 2D Illustrator ornaments into 3D with Maya 2015 for printing
• Organized schedules for students to use the HIVE and other facilities to print their 3D ornaments
• Worked with my teammate Allan Bangera to initialize a reminder system using MailChimp
• Used MailChimp to send instructions and links to our file database to students and faculty
• Collaborated with faculty to get maximum student participation (We met our goal of 65 ornaments and then some) 
The project was a success! And now CITYarts has made a book of our students' ornaments that were printed! (See link below)

Also did research for expanding our undergraduate BFA curriculum, in which my responsibilities were: 
• Revise Google Sheets spreadsheet into cohesive format 
• Research 5 colleges for specific undergrad degrees that we were interested in and add them to the spreadsheet for faculty conference

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:

• Served as photographer for 2015's Kid 2 College session

volunteerExperiences.description: Spoke to NYIT EMBA Chinese students beginning their journey at NYIT in the US. I spoke to them about how important it is to get outside of your comfortable cohort and talk to as many people from other cultures as possible. Doing so really gives you a leg up in the business world, I believe. That's the message I wanted to convey to them.

As President of NYIT's GEO, the team and I organized and hosted the Fair Trade Festival at our school to raise money for developing countries. Artisans from those countries sent us their handcrafted work via Ten Thousand Villages in which we sold here and sent the money back to them. It was an amazing experience getting to learn more about different cultures. Each item had a cultural story behind it. See pictures here: https://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.549962765140057.1073741833.541273556008978&type=3#

projects.title: GEO Communication Network
projects.description:
Currently my team and I are building a communication network on behalf of our NYIT club, GEO (Global Exchange Organization). The project will attempt to connect students from our global universities in China to our American/domestic students so that they build a comfortability and relationship before either party studies abroad.
The system will match students based on common interest so there will be common ground for the conversations to start.

projects.title: Hassh Digital
projects.description:
With a small team we're building a platform that delivers cutting-edge web development and peer-reviewed tech research as news to educate our audience in a time of fake media. 

We're using the following to create our platform: 
• JIRA/Bitbucket/Basecamp 3 (Project Management)
• HTML/SASS/Angular 2/Nunjucks/Gulp (Dev languages)

S/N: We're also working on finding out how Facebook pixels work, and how we can use data driven ad research to promote our brand (and hopefully make a little profit)

organizations.name: GEO (Global Exchange Organization)
organizations.description:
Founder and President of GEO

• Organized a group of members to serve as the executive board
• Reached out to various clubs and organizations to collaborate events and ideas with
• Organized the database and structured it for successors and accessibility
• Created responsive email newsletters, event posters and response templates
• Designed brand logo and most of the promotional graphics for social media
• Generated relationship with our club and respective department heads to ensure the success of our events
• Created a legacy that could be passed down to future members

Since NYIT is considered a "Global University" due to its many campuses across the world and its vast international and multicultural student body, GEO has been created to close the gap between international students and domestic students on campus through various activities and events which will bring both parties together. 

International students on campus can often be seen in groups of their own and not getting the best out of their experience abroad by mingling and doing much work with the domestic students due to possible language or culture gaps. GEO aims to tackle those issues firsthand and help NYIT become a truly "Global" university.

volunteerExperience.description: Spoke to NYIT EMBA Chinese students beginning their journey at NYIT in the US. I spoke to them about how important it is to get outside of your comfortable cohort and talk to as many people from other cultures as possible. Doing so really gives you a leg up in the business world, I believe. That's the message I wanted to convey to them.

As President of NYIT's GEO, the team and I organized and hosted the Fair Trade Festival at our school to raise money for developing countries. Artisans from those countries sent us their handcrafted work via Ten Thousand Villages in which we sold here and sent the money back to them. It was an amazing experience getting to learn more about different cultures. Each item had a cultural story behind it. See pictures here: https://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.549962765140057.1073741833.541273556008978&type=3#
